title: Crewship panel payload — series.v1
description: Named series over shared category labels, rendered as a grouped bar chart (bar is the only form in v1; line and area are v1.1). Pushed by a routine or by a script running inside a crew container. Three rules from §3 are structural rather than advisory and are visible in the shape below: ONE UNIT per panel — `unit` is a single required scalar and a series object has no unit field of its own, because dual axes are the most common chart error and cannot be defended at render time; MAX 5 SERIES — a sixth is merged into an "other" series rather than refused, so a producer that grows a dimension keeps pushing and the chart stays inside the five-colour palette; and colour belongs to the ENTITY, so the renderer keys colour off `name` and never off a series' position in this array. The server attaches the timestamp, the run id and the producer identity; freshness is computed from the timestamp the server stored, which is why there is no field here for a producer to supply one.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (informational; the server ignores it). Present so a hand-written payload gets inline validation in an editor while a producer script is being developed.

unit.description: The one unit every value on this panel is measured in ("ms", "req/s", "Kč"). Required and singular: §3 says one unit per panel, and two units is two panels. A compound unit that is genuinely one unit is fine — "req/s", "MB/day" — but a string that names two ("ms and %", "Kč, ks", "count | rate") is refused at the boundary, because that is the dual-axis error arriving through the only door left open to it.

items.description: One category on the shared axis. Plain text; the renderer truncates what will not fit and keeps the full string in a tooltip.

labels.description: The categories, in render order — the producer sorts, because the panel has no query with which to sort anything. Every series carries exactly one value per label, in this order. Bounded at 50: past that the bars are thinner than their gaps and the honest rendering is a table.

series.description: The series. Up to five are drawn in their own colour; from the sixth on they are summed element-wise into a single series named "other" (§3), which is a rendering rule and not a rejection — a producer whose dimension grew from four values to nine keeps pushing and keeps getting a readable chart. Bounded at 24 on the wire so the merge itself stays cheap; a producer with more than twenty-four series is aggregating in the wrong place.

Series.description: One named series. There is no `unit` here, and that absence is the enforcement of "one unit per panel" — the shape gives a producer nowhere to put a second one. There is no `color` here either: colour belongs to the entity and is derived from `name` by the renderer, so a filter that removes a series cannot recolour the rest, and a producer cannot spend a reserved status colour on a series.

name.description: The entity this series measures, and its identity for the whole render: the legend text, the direct label, and the key the colour is derived from. Unique within the payload — two series sharing a name would share a colour and a legend row, and the second would be unreadable. "other" is a legal name; if the payload declares one, the overflow from the sixth series on is folded into it rather than becoming a second row with the same name.

items.description: One data point, in the panel's unit. `0` is a measured zero and draws a bar of zero height labelled `0`; `null` is no basis to compute and draws no bar at all, labelled with an em dash (§9b.4). The two are different claims and the renderer keeps them apart per point, so a gap in one series never reads as a floor.

values.description: One value per label, in the same order as `labels`, and exactly as many. The server checks the two lengths agree — JSON Schema cannot cross-reference them, and a short array would silently shift every bar after the gap onto the wrong category.
